 SCCH-24 2 MVC 3910/2020  :J U D G M E N T:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 10-03-2020 at about 4-30 a.m., the petitioner was driving Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-04-X- 3390 on Chandragiri-Renigunta road.

When he reached near G.Ramanappa Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/
1 Gandhinagar, Tirupathi Rural Mandal, at that time the driver of APSRTC bus bearing reg.No.AP-03-Z-5640 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the petitioner's tractor on its rear side, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to S.V.R.R.G.R (Ruya) Hospital Tirupathi wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 10-03-2020 to 18- 03-2020.
So far the petitioner has spent huge amount for treatment.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He is aged about 32 years and was working as a driver.
Apart from that he was doing agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.30, 000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. Respondent- the RC owner cum insurer of APSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.AP-09-Z-5640 has filed the written statement and questioned the jurisdiction of this Tribunal to try the matter.
It is further contended that the offending bus is not at all involved in the accident and there was no rash or negligent act on the part of the driver of offending bus.

It is further contended that on 9-03- 2020,
the driver of said APSRTC bus started from Bangalore to Tirupathi on its regular route.
When the bus reached near Gandhinagar, Tirupathi Rural Mandal on Chandragiri Renigunta road, at about 4-30 a.m., on 10- 03-2020, there was an accident.

In that accident the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-04-X-3390 has dashed his Tractor to the road median line/road divider which is at the height of 1 to 1 1/2 feet and the driver of Tractor was fallen on the road divider which is about 5 to 6 ft in width in between the 6 line National Highway which is measuring about 150 ft. vide road.

There was no light or signal or even radium reflector stick to the body of the Trailer of the Tractor and some people are watching the incident which was happened just 10-15 minutes before the arrival of the APSRTC bus at the place of accident.

4. It is further contended that the driver of the was under the influence of Alcohol and who was talking over the mobile by using ear phone has dashed to the right side road median result of which Tractor toppled to his right side and he has fallen on the road median.
It is further contended that the petitioner/driver of the Tractor has no valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle has no permit and FC to ply on the road as on the date of accident.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a motor vehicle accident on 10-03- 2020 at about 4-30 a.m., near Gandhinagar, Tirupathi Rural Mandal on Chandragiri- Renigunta road, Andhrapradesh and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of APSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.AP-03-Z-5640?
2. Whether this Tribunal has territorial jurisdiction to try the petition?
G.Ramanappa
Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/
2 3. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?
6. In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.
The respondent has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.

7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue no 3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
:REASONS:
9. Issue No.2 : The respondent has seriously disputed the jurisdiction of this court to try the petition.

According to the respondent, the accident in question has occurred near GandhiNagar, Tirupathi Rural Mandal, on Chandragiri -Ranegunta road, Andhar Pradesh District and the petitioner is the permanent resident of Diguva Gorrala Doddi, Pasupathuru, Gangavaram, Gundagulla, Chittoor District of Andhra Pradesh and the registered owner of the APSRTC bus is the Manager Director,
APSRTC, Central office, RTC house, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.
Hence, no part of cause of action has taken place in Bangalore i.e., within the jurisdiction of this Court.
Hence this court has no jurisdiction to try the petition.
10. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent, if the materials placed on record are perused, it is true that the accident in question has occurred at Andhra Pradesh District.
The petitioners are the residence of Andhra Pradesh District and the Head office of respondent is at Andhra Pradesh District.

The petitioner has arrayed the Senior Traffic Manager APSRTC,
Kempegowda bus station, Tank Bund road, Subashnagar, Majestic, Bangalore as respondent.

sentences.text:
The respondent has contended that the Senior Traffic Inspector, APSRTC Branch, Subashnagar,
Majestic, Bangalore is not the registered owner, hence petition is bad for mis-joinder and non - joinder of proper and necessary parties.
11. If the case sheet is perused, summons was issued to the respondent to the address mentioned in the cause title of the petition.

The said notice was duly served to the Assistant Manager (Traffic)
APSRTC Bangalore point as there is endorsement of Assistant Manager (Traffic) APSRTC Bangalore regarding the due service of summons.
In response to the summons, the respondent has engaged the service of panel advocate to represent their case.

It is not disputed by the respondent that they G.Ramanappa Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/
3 have Branch office at Bangalore even though the Head office is at Vijayawada, Andra Pradesh.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment reported in (2016) 3 SCC 43 between Malati Sardar Vs. National Insurance Limited & Ors., wherein referring the question raised in the said case regarding the territorial jurisdiction of Tribunal under Sec. 166 (2) has observed that though claimant is residing outside its jurisdiction but respondent Insurance Company carrying on business within its jurisdiction hence claim petition before such Tribunal is maintainable.

entities.text: Malati Sardar Vs. National Insurance Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that Sec. 166 being a benevolent provision, provision for territorial jurisdiction must be interpreted consistent with object of facilitating remedies for victims and any hyper technical approach should be avoided.

No bar to claim petition being filed where insurance company, which is main contesting party in such cases has its business since neither any prejudice is caused to party nor is there failure of justice.

12. Considering the observation made in the aforesaid judgment so also the fact that the business of respondent is running even at Bangalore which is within the jurisdiction this court, it can be said without any hesitation that this court has jurisdiction to try the case.
Hence, issue no.2 is answered in the affirmative.

13. Issue no.1 : - In order to prove the case and thereby to prove that rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle itself is the sole cause for accident, the petitioner has given his evidence as PW.1.
It is deposed by PW.1 that on 10-03-2020 at about 4-30 a.m., he was driving the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP-04-X- 3390 on Chandragiri-Renigunta road.

When he reached near Gandhinagar, Tirupathi Rural Mandal, at that time the driver of APSRTC bus bearing reg.No.AP-03-Z-5640 (hereinafter referred to as the offending the vehicle) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the tractor from back side, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries..

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
14.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 which are the police records such as F.I.R, complaint,
translated copy of complaint, wound certificate, sketch, IMV report, charge sheet etc.,
15.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by G Chakravathi, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No 72/2020 of Mutyalareddypalli Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279,
338 of IPC.
16.

Though the respondent has contended that their vehicle is not involved in the accident and that it is prior to their vehicle plied through the said road itself the accident in question has occurred but if the entire materials placed on record is carefully perused, it can be said that offending vehicle did involved in the accident.

It is true that the petitioner has not produced the IMV report to let the court know the damages caused to the vehicles involved in the accident but if really no damage was caused to the offending vehicle then the respondent could have produced the IMV report to substantiate their contention.

If the sketch is perused, the accident in question has occurred on the G.Ramanappa Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/
4 left side of the road.
The offending vehicle which came from the same direction in which the petitioner was proceeding hit to the vehicle of the petitioner from behind.
If the respondent had maintained minimum distance between the two vehicles this accident could have been avoided.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
Hence, issue no.2 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P3 and 4.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at SVRRGG Hospital, Tirupati from 10-03-2020 to 18-03-2020 for a period of 9 days.

As per wound certificate,
the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.

18. Dr.Shailesh A V Rao -Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2 and through him OPD records, Neuro Psychological Assessment report, Mini Mental State Examination report, are got marked as per Ex.P 10 to 12.
The P.W.2 has deposed that the petitioner consulted him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 07-08-2024 and on 19-08-2024 for the assessment of disability.
PW.2 further deposed that the neuro psychological Assessment of petitioner was done, his IQ was 42 (90-109).
He is below average in thinking and reasoning and has moderate mental retardation.
On IDEAS, he obtained a score 07, indicating moderate disability of 40-70%.
His MMSE score is 15/30 which is low score.
PW.2 further deposed that he has assessed the disability as per the disability Assessment and Certification Guidelines issued by DGHS, GOI during 2001 and 2018.
On the modified Rankin Scale, the petitioner has score of 1.
As per the guidelines, this amounts to a disability of around 20%.
19. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, admittedly he is not a treated doctor.
The petitioner has not undergone any surgery.
As per the wound certificate petitioner has sustained abrasion injury of 2x2 cm and there was blood oozing from ES.
The PW.2 except verifying the discharge summary has not verified the case sheet.
He has not verified any document for the follow up treatment if any taken by the petitioner.
It is admitted by PW.2 that he was not present at the time of treatment given by neurophysiologist and that none of the document discloses the type of treatment given by neurophysiologist.

It is admitted by PW.2 that there is no document to prove that because of the head injury sustained by the petitioner it has adversely affected him and admitted that none of the medical documents discloses that the petitioner has headache and his memory power is lessened.

20. If the evidence of PW.1 is perused, he has given rational answer to the entire question posed to him without any hindrance even for a while and cleverly has given answer to the entire question posed to him and it is he who himself has represented the case without his being represented through guardian.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in MFA No.9065/2019 c/w MFA No.3748/2019 between Raghugowda Vs. The Mangaing Director,
BMTC, wherein, in the similar set of facts the doctor has reported that petitioner has sustained 50%
disability but the court while observing that the petitioner has filed application on his own and as a normal person he has prosecuted the petition, he has given evidence on his own and he is a normal person with normal intellect has observed that petitioner has not suffered any disability and only with a view to get higher compensation, he has chosen to produce a false report and PW.2 being a G.Ramanappa Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/

sentences.text: 5 responsible doctor has not only given a false report but also given evidence on oath based on such false report has decline to consider the percentage of disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner.
21. The observation made in the aforesaid ruling is aptly applicable to the case in hand.
Hence, this court declines to consider the evidence of PW.2 and intern declines to consider the neurological disability assessed by the PW.2.

When petitioner has sustained head injury and underwent surgery,
under such circumstances because of the head injury suffered by him it may have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of future income.
22. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
23. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.

24. Further for 9 days of hospitalization at SVRRGG Hospital, Tirupati and for his taking follow up treatment in the said hospitals, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/-.
25.
It is submitted by the petitioner that he was working as driver, apart from that he was also doing agricultural work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.14,000/- p.m.
26.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for two month.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.28,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
27. The petitioner at his age of 32 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Sl. Heads Amount No.
1.
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 60,000/-
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
G.Ramanappa
Alias Ramana vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102862037/
6  charges and nourishing food 3.

Medical expenses - 4. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 28,000/-
 period 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs.1,00,000/-

Total Rs.2,13,000/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,13,000/- ( Rupees Two Lakh Thirteen Thousand only).
28. As regarding liability is concerned, the Respondent being the RC owner cum insured of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 3 is answered.
29. Issue No.4: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total  compensation of Rs.2,13,000/- + cost of Rs.2,000/- imposed vide order dated 24-09- 2024.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,15,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifteen Thousand only).
A Sum of Rs.2,13,000/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 7th day of November 2024.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl., SCJ & ACJM., Bengaluru.
